# PLAN — iteration 2

## Current state assessment

Iteration 1 preserved behavior and passed the verification gates, but routed use stayed at 4 LUTs and 5 FFs, so it did not improve on the timing-feasible incumbent. Its top-local registered implementation is equivalent to the frozen child and synthesis flattens the hierarchy; repeating that approach would not address the failed objective gate.

## Hypothesis

Track only consecutive samples that differ from the registered `clean` value, eliminating the separate `candidate` register and potentially reducing FF use from 5 to 4 while preserving the 8th-edge output change.

## Instruction for generator

Replace the child instance with top-local logic containing registered `clean` and a 3-bit run counter; keep the matching `// @latency 0` annotation. On synchronous active-high reset, clear both registers; when `noisy == clean`, clear the counter, and when `noisy != clean`, increment it unless it is already 7, in which case update `clean` to `noisy` and clear the counter. This must change `clean` on the eighth consecutive differing sample, with interruptions restarting the count; preserve the ports and registered output behavior.
